caption:
Toto stretches around every run, but his hamstrings feel tight again soon after.

Hamstrings can feel tight because they're working hard to stabilise, not because they're too short. They need to stay strong as they lengthen, like when you bend forward or sprint.

Clinical Pilates trains this with slow, controlled movement. Start with bridges, feet on a box or reformer bar, lowering over three seconds. Ten steady reps beats thirty rushed ones. Then progress to single-leg bridges. Enjoy stretching? Keep it, and pair it with strength work two or three times a week.

Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio can build a program for your sport. Book online via the link in bio.
